Heard Sri. M. P. Nanaiah, learned Senior counsel for Sri. Tumbigi Prabhugouda Basavantarayagouda, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri. V. S. Vinayaka, learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent-State.
2. Present petition is filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C.
3.

The brief facts of the case are as under:
A complaint came to be filed by the victim lady with Sanjay Nagar Police Station on 10.01.2023 which was registered in Crime No.3/2023 for the offences punishable under Sections 354, 376 and 511 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (hereinafter referred to as 'IPC' for short).
4. Gist of the complaint averments reveals that victim lady aged about 24 years was resident of Chattisghad State and after completing her graduation in the Business Management, she responded to a Assistant Executive post for which the advertisement is issued by Raj Builders Private Limited,
Bengaluru.
She was asked to appear in-person on 10.01.2023.
Accordingly, she came to Bengaluru on 09.01.2023 at about 7.30 p.m., to Yeshwanthapura railway station.
She was informed by the company that she would be picked up from the railway station in the car belonging to the company and accordingly, she boarded the car.
She was informed that she would be housed in the company guest house.
Thereafter, she was picked up in the car from the railway station and taken to the company guest house.
She was asked to fresh up and stay in the Guest House.

The complainant had her friends in Bengaluru while she was pursuing her education and she contacted them and thereafter, her friend also joined her in the car and they had food and thereafter, her friend was dropped to her place and the complainant was brought back to the guest house.
5. Petitioner at that point of time, asked the complainant to come to his room and in the room,

The attempt said to have been made to commit rape on the complainant, is resisted by the complainant and she took shelter in the neighbouring flat and thereafter called her friend and her friend came and she got rescued and thereafter, she lodged a complaint with the police.
6. Police after registering the case, are investigated the matter thoroughly inter-alia arrested the petitioner and sent him to judicial custody and after thorough investigation, police filed the charge sheet.

7. The attempt made by the petitioner to obtain an order of grant of bail was turned down by the LIII Additional City Civil and Sessions Special Judge, Bengaluru by order dated 15.02.2023 in Crl.
Misc. No.859/2023.

sentences.text: Thereafter, the petitioner is before this Court.

8. Sri. M. P. Nanaiah, learned Senior counsel representing the petitioner reiterating the grounds urged in the bail petition vehemently contended that even according to the charge sheet materials,
at the most, the action i.e., attributable to the petitioner is that of attempt to rape as there is no materials on record which would attract the offence punishable under Section 375 of IPC.
9.

He also contended that in the charge sheet itself there is a mention that the statement of the victim lady is recorded before the jurisdictional Magistrate under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. but the same is not made as part of the charge sheet material and therefore, made a request to the Court that the said statement be secured from the concerned Court for the purpose of appreciation of the bail grounds.
Accordingly, this Court directed the Registry to secure the statement from XXVII ACMM, Bengaluru.

10. In pursuance of the directions issued by this Court, the statement of the victim lady recorded on 16.01.2023 by the XXVII ACMM, Bengaluru is secured in a sealed cover and the same is perused by this Court.

11. This Court is satisfied from such statement that the stand taken up by the accused petitioner that it was only an attempt to rape and not exactly the rape as is defined under Section 375 of IPC.
12.
The report was also made available to the learned HCGP for perusal.
13. On such perusal, learned HCGP submitted that the statement of the victim lady would not run contrary to the grounds urged in the petition.
14. However, learned HCGP opposes that the materials on record would attract the offence under Section 354A of IPC at the least and therefore, petitioner is not entitled for grant of bail.
15. In the light of the rival contentions, this Court perused the materials on record meticulously.
16. On such perusal of the materials on record, it is seen that the incident said to have occurred in the intervening night of 09th and 10th January 2023.

sentences.text: job of Assistance Executive in the petitioner company reached Bengaluru by train to Yeshwanthpura railway station at about 7.30 p.m. from Chattisghad State.
17. The complainant was picked up by the petitioner company's car and was brought to the alleged guest house of the petitioner's company.
18. As could be seen from the complaint averments, the unfortunate incident said to have occurred in the intervening night of 9th and 10th January, 2023.

As could be seen from the complaint averments, the complainant got escaped from the clutches of the petitioner and took shelter in the neighbouring flat and later on called her friend and moved with him and took shelter with her friend that night and next day morning she has lodged the complaint with the jurisdictional police.

19. Even assuming that the entire contents of the complaint are to be true for the sake of arguments,
as is rightly contended on behalf of the petitioner Sri. M. P. Nanaiah, learned Senior counsel, the act attributable by the petitioner to be one punishable under Section 354A of IPC at the most.

20. Further, perusal of the content of the statement recorded by the XXVII ACMM, Bengaluru on 16.01.2023 under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. of victim lady, at the request of Investigating Agency would not make out any further improvement in the case of the prosecution.
Anyway, it is for the learned trial Judge to find out what exactly is the offence that has been committed by the accused petitioner after full fledged trial and award appropriate punishment.

21. It is too pre-mature for this Court to form any opinion as to the merits or demerits of the case by holding a mini trial as the same may prejudice the case of the parties during the trial one way or the other.
22. Suffice to say that the materials available on record at this stage do not warrant continuation of the accused petitioner in judicial custody any longer.

23. The apprehension of the prosecution can be met with by imposing stringent and suitable conditions, accordingly, this Court passes the following:
ORDER 1.
The Criminal Petition is allowed.
